Chicken Dump

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
An accredited and well-known Chicken Abattoir in Potchefstroom is dumping chicken offal and waste... everywhere!

Unique Selling Point:
Undercover footage shows a well-known chicken abattoir in Potchefstroom breaking a variety of health and safety regulations, polluting the environment and mistreating their staff. From dumping chicken waste and offal in the veld, to poor recycling of waste water, to staff working in dismal, unhygienic circumstances... Crest Choice Chicken seems to be cutting corners to maximise profits. Their trucks are not roadworthy, staff have no working toilets, plastic bags being burnt onsite, blood running through the yard, the wastewater dam is constantly overflowing - even into the workshop. Bloodied wastewater is used to wash the floors of the abattoir and sprayed on the adjacent field. The entire area looks like a scrapyard.

Summary:
A group of workers from Crest Choice Chicken have had enough. They are being bullied by the owners, forced to work overtime without pay, and subjected to disgusting and unsafe working conditions. They have collected evidence of the company's transgressions over the past few months, from blood and waste on the floors, to burning plastic and rotten chicken offal being dumped in the veld.

How can an accredited abattoir, supplying major retailers get away with this kind of behaviour?

Further information:
Crest Choice Chicken is a family-owned poultry operation that was established in 1995. We started supplying Potchefstroom’s local major retailer from day one and the relationship has now spanned 25 years. Crest Choice Chicken started off from humble beginnings, with a 500 birds per day operation and just 50 employees. Today, we are an internationally recognised FSSC 22000 facility with more than 600 employees and produce over 30 000 birds per day. From fresh to frozen, crumbed to value-added products, Crest Choice Chicken produces over 50 different article lines. We are proud to supply the fresh poultry market with approximately 7 000 000 birds each year.

Locations:
Potchefstroom

Cell video and photos of conditions on the plant and the dumping of the chicken

Press Release:


A truck reverses onto a veld outside Potchefstroom, tipping its contents into a shallow quarry – chicken offal from a nearby abattoir. But it’s not the first time an accredited chicken abattoir supplying major retailers has ruffled feathers: insiders have long accused it of unhygienic and unsafe working conditions. Carte Blanche investigates whether there’s substance to claims this well-known brand is intent on cutting corners. 
Producer: Stenette Grosskopf | Research: Laura Byrne | Presenter: Claire Mawisa 

Script:


CHICKEN DUMP – MASTER
V/O
This is Crest Choice Chicken, a poultry processing operation situated just outside Potchefstroom in the North West Province. Here the company has a high throughput chicken abattoir and a rendering plant that processes abattoir waste into animal feed.
LINK
According to their website, Crest Choice Chicken has been in operation for 25 years, and today they are an internationally recognised facility, producing 30 000 birds per day.
V/O
And the meat from these chickens is sold at various outlets countrywide, including their own chain of butcheries throughout the province… and even nationally… at Pick n Pay retail…

But it seems behind the high-class website and professional-looking exterior, lurk some dark secrets…
Makokota
We are not satisfied, all the people that I'm working with.
Thabiso
The environment is not healthy, is not good.
John
I complained once and they told me there’s the gate…
Peter
Dis net haglike omstandighede…

It’s just dire conditions.
V/O
These men work at the plant – employed by Crest Choice Chicken’s subcontractors. It’s late on a Saturday afternoon when we meet, and they’ve been working a long six-day week. They agree to speak to us as long as we hide their identity – scared of the repercussions of speaking out on what they say are unhealthy, illegal and unethical business practices where they work…
Peter
Die mense is nie gelukkig nie maar dis hulle brood en botter en dis die manier hoe hulle vir hulle families sorg. Hulle is afhanklik van dit…

The people are not happy but it’s their bread and butter and it’s the way they provide for their families. They depend on it.
V/O
This worker – we’ll call him Peter – says poor hygiene is evident around the abattoir, adding that bloody, dirty water often flows through the yard…
Peter
Baie keer oorvloei die verepit en dan’s al daai water op ons terrein – waar ons moet werk en ons moet loop.

Often the feather pit overflows. Then all that water ends up on our terrain, where we must work and walk.
John
Sometimes you still find the chicken’s heads laying around there on the premises….
V/O
A worker we’ve named John believes the filthy water has affected his health…
John
We don’t have much of a choice but to work in the water.

Claire: You’re working in the water that’s dirty?

Yes,

Claire: And contaminated…

Yes.
V/o
Thabiso – also not his real name – spends long hours at the abattoir, and says the filth and smell are almost too much to bear.

This skip, placed in the yard is often filled with burning chicken waste and plastic…
Thabiso
They are burning the feathers, the blood and what not… it’s stinking, stinking the whole day.
V/O
In South Africa, abattoirs are regulated by various pieces of fragmented legislation… but hygiene and waste disposal specifically, are enforced by Provincial Government.
Dr Langa Madyibi
Veterinary Services basically monitors compliance of abattoirs to the Meat Safety Act.
V/O
Our producer sits down with Dr Langa Madyibi – the Director of Veterinary Services at the North West Department of Agriculture and Land Reform. We need to understand how these seemingly dire conditions were allowed to continue under his watch…
Dr Langa Madyibi
Are you familiar with Crest Choice Chicken in Potchefstroom?

Yes I am familiar with Crest Choice.

Have you been to the facility yourself?

Not personally…
V/O
We show him the video of the burning waste in the skip, wondering if this is considered acceptable waste management at an abattoir…
Dr Langa Madyibi
Burning is generally not looked at favourably also for environmentally related reasons. The one method that is generally recommended is what they have there - rendering…
V/O
Crest Choice’s rendering plant is supposed to process the abattoir waste into animal feed, but according to this man – who wants to be called Makokota – a lot of waste never makes it to the plant …
Makokota
Those things they put it in the blue drum, the blue drums they put the intestines. And the intestines when they get hot they burst and overflow the drum like this…
V/O
And when the drums overflow, Makakota and others often end up cleaning the mess…
Makokota
You can’t pick it up with a spade or something else. You can’t pick it up like that. You have to take it with your hands like this.


V/O
Despite all the allegations, Crest Choice Chicken believes it is fully compliant with the law – they told us that they’ve had TWO unannounced inspections since our investigation began… and nothing out of the ordinary was found… and Dr Madyibi agrees…
Madyibi
Yes, it’s true. I have records of those inspections, which, yes they have tried to comply… They have in fact complied… let me not put them down…
V/O
But the problems at Crest Choice Chicken have not gone away…
Thabiso
The toilets are a mess. The sewage on the whole is a mess.
Peter
Okay, kom ek wys vir jou hoe lyk ons toilette.

Claire: Aaag, NO!

Ek het ‘n vergadering gehad met die einaar, met al die belanghebbendes rondom daai toilet.

Claire: I can’t even.
Madyibi
So how do you comply when this is what your bathroom looks like?

That’s not compliance with hygiene. It’s a pity… I, I didn’t go there personally myself. But… it’s possible that that part of the infrastructure, that building was not inspected properly…
LINK
This Channel flows from the Abattoir premises to the mooirivier spruit, and joins the vaal river about 20kms downstream… So when it does rain all the blood and the offal from the abattoir flows right through here… keep on recording…
V/O
Within minutes of us arriving outside the Crest Choice Premises, we’re approached by guards, claiming we’re trespassing.
Claire:
Private property, Boetie, it starts on the other side of the fence. So, I’m not inside the property right now. Please let them know, okay?
V/O
And as we leave, we come across this truck delivering chickens to the abattoir. …

And the staff transport isn’t much better, according to those working at the plant. A lot of them live in Rammulotsi, a township in Viljoenskroon, 40kms away just across the Free State border. They rely on these company buses that take them to and from work each day…
Thabiso
Handles of the doors of the buses, its like the door of the house… the shooter, that handle that you open it with when you lock your house. It’s home-made.
Peter
Claire: Why do you still work there?

Ek het vir lank sonder werk gesit. Ek is oor 50 en jy kry nie maklik werk nie. Dit is die rede. As jy ‘n rukkie sonder werk sit en dit begin swaar gaan dan vat jy wat jy kry.

I was unemployed for a long time. I am over 50 and you don’t find work easily. That is the reason. If you’re unemployed for a while and you start to struggle, then you take what you get.
V/O


Since our investigation started “Peter” has been dismissed from his job… for speaking out on practices he feels are breaking the law… And one practice, in particular, is truly shocking…
Peter
Die veevoerfabriek het overstock geraak en toe moet hulle die goed wegry en toe het ek gesien hulle dump dit in n boer se quarry.

The rendering plant became overstocked and then they had to dispose of the waste. Then I saw they’re dumping it in a farmer’s quarry.
V/O
This is where the excess abattoir waste from Crest Choice Chicken ends up… Dumped in a pit on a farm right next to the Vaal river.
V/O
We share the footage of the dumped chicken waste with Cormac Cullinan, senior environmental lawyer and director of South Africa’s oldest specialist environmental and green business law firm.
Cormac Cullinan
I was appalled to see that kind of behavior. It's deeply antisocial behavior. Basically, you have private companies saving themselves a lot of money by polluting the environment that we all share…
Claire: The owners say that the footage that we have is part of a process and we’re not getting the bigger picture, we didn’t see the entire process of what’s happening. What is your reaction to that?
I’m afraid that’s laughable. There is no lawful process that involves dumping huge amounts of chicken waste into the veld.
V/O
Dr Madyibi too is shocked by what he sees…
Dr Langa Madyibi
There are specified methods to dispose of that waste, and dumping it like that is not one of the specified methods.
V/O
He says that Veterinary Services do consider alternative waste disposal methods, but an abattoir needs to apply for permission which is carefully assessed before approval is granted..
Dr Langa Madyibi
Off the head, I would not approve that. I also do not have a protocol that has been submitted to my office that seeks to approve disposal of waste like that.
V/O
We contacted Crest Choice Chicken for an interview but the company’s lawyers responded to the allegations in writing…
They deny any wrongdoing and state that the company has consistently scored highly on the Department’s waste management’s requirements. The allegations, they say, are simply unsubstantiated and false claims from a disgruntled employee of a subcontractor …and that the company is the victim of sabotage…
The skip with burning waste – Crest Choice’s response is that they stopped this practice – on request from the Department – approximately 2 years ago… But these images were filmed in April this year…
When it comes to the toilets, they blame the occasional blockage on ignorance – workers using too much toilet paper.
They are also not aware of any defects on the company buses and trucks, saying the vehicles regularly go through roadworthy tests.
And then there is the matter of dumping abattoir waste in the veld.
Crest Choice says the dumped waste is considered non-hazardous organic material and one does not need a permit to bury it as it will not cause any environmental harm…
But they are wrong… We’re informed abattoir waste is condemned material and it must be disposed of according to government regulations.
Cormac Cullinan
Particularly when you talk about meats and rotten substances like that, they can have very bad effects on water resources in a number of ways.


Crest Choice Chicken also categorically denies dumping blue drums …. saying they’d be reused…
Yet the footage recorded in April clearly shows the drums being off-loaded with the waste… And we went back almost three months later – the rotting chicken waste and blue drums were still there, exactly where they left them…
Cormac Cullinan
We’re talking about a situation where the law can impose criminal penalties, not only on the company, but even on directors and senior managers who fail to take the right measures to address this and to ensure that this kind of pollution and unlawful disposal does not happen.
V/O
The local municipality and the Green Scorpions have launched an investigation into some of the practices at Crest Choice Chicken, but the workers we spoke to are wondering what that will mean for them…
Peter
Why did you feel the need to share this story? What was sitting on your heart for you to want to let people know what the conditions are there?

Ek kry die mense jammer wat moet so werk. En oor jy geld het en geld maak beteken nie jy kan die environment verniel nie…

I feel sorry for the people who have to work like that. And because you have money, and make money, it doesn’t mean that you can destroy the environment.








PROMO 1 11”
Allegations of unhygienic premises and illicit waste management practices…

UPSOUND: There’s no way that that can possibly be legal…

We investigate an abattoir that seems to be sidestepping the law.


PROMO 2 21”
Truckloads of chicken waste dumped in a veld…

UPSOUND: It's deeply antisocial behavior.

Unhappy employees who have to endure unhygienic and unsafe working conditions…

UPSOUND: Sometimes you still find the chicken’s heads laying around there on the premises….

We investigate the goings-on at a poultry abattoir in the North West…
PROMO 3 21”
Do you think about where your chicken on the braai comes from? Or what happened to the feathers, innards and scraps from the abattoir?

UPSOUND: These types of activities are deeply antisocial. You’re basically prepared to take the risk of poisoning water that other people, other animals will drink…

We investigate a poultry abattoir that seems to think dumping waste in the veld is lawful and ethical…




PROMO 4 21”
It’s an accredited chicken abattoir which supplies major retailers.

UPSOUND: Ons grootste plek vir wie ons voorsien is Pick n Pay — Pick n Pay as ’n groep…


VO:
But disturbing undercover footage shows how this well-known business in Potchestroom, is cutting corners to maximise profits

UPSOUND: It's deeply antisocial behaviour.

The allegations, they say, are simply unsubstantiated and false claims from a disgruntled employee of a subcontractor …and that the company is the victim of sabotage… The skip with burning waste – Crest Choice’s response is that they stopped this practice – on request from the Department – approximately 2 years ago… But these images were filmed in April this year… When it comes to the toilets, they blame the occasional blockage on ignorance – workers using too much toilet paper. They are also not aware of any defects on the company buses and trucks, saying the vehicles regularly go through roadworthy tests. And then there is the matter of dumping abattoir waste in the veld. Crest Choice says the dumped waste is considered non-hazardous organic material and one does not need a permit to bury it as it will not cause any environmental harm… But they are wrong… We’re informed abattoir waste is condemned material and it must be disposed of according to government regulations. Cormac Cullinan Particularly when you talk about meats and rotten substances like that, they can have very bad effects on water resources in a number of ways. Crest Choice Chicken also categorically denies dumping blue drums …. saying they’d be reused… Yet the footage recorded in April clearly shows the drums being off-loaded with the waste… And we went back almost three months later – the rotting chicken waste and blue drums were still there, exactly where they left them… Cormac Cullinan We’re talking about a situation where the law can impose criminal penalties, not only on the company, but even on directors and senior managers who fail to take the right measures to address this and to ensure that this kind of pollution and unlawful disposal does not happen. What was sitting on your heart for you to want to let people know what the conditions are there? Ek kry die mense jammer wat moet so werk. En oor jy geld het en geld maak beteken nie jy kan die environment verniel nie… I feel sorry for the people who have to work like that. And because you have money, and make money, it doesn’t mean that you can destroy the environment. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): An accredited and well-known Chicken Abattoir in Potchefstroom is dumping chicken offal and waste... everywhere!
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Undercover footage shows a well-known chicken abattoir in Potchefstroom breaking a variety of health and safety regulations, polluting the environment and mistreating their staff. From dumping chicken waste and offal in the veld, to poor recycling of waste water, to staff working in dismal, unhygienic circumstances... Crest Choice Chicken seems to be cutting corners to maximise profits. Their trucks are not roadworthy, staff have no working toilets, plastic bags being burnt onsite, blood running through the yard, the wastewater dam is constantly overflowing - even into the workshop. Bloodied wastewater is used to wash the floors of the abattoir and sprayed on the adjacent field. The entire area looks like a scrapyard.
metadata.Summary: A group of workers from Crest Choice Chicken have had enough. They are being bullied by the owners, forced to work overtime without pay, and subjected to disgusting and unsafe working conditions. They have collected evidence of the company's transgressions over the past few months, from blood and waste on the floors, to burning plastic and rotten chicken offal being dumped in the veld. How can an accredited abattoir, supplying major retailers get away with this kind of behaviour?
metadata.Further information: Crest Choice Chicken is a family-owned poultry operation that was established in 1995. We started supplying Potchefstroom’s local major retailer from day one and the relationship has now spanned 25 years. Crest Choice Chicken started off from humble beginnings, with a 500 birds per day operation and just 50 employees. Today, we are an internationally recognised FSSC 22000 facility with more than 600 employees and produce over 30 000 birds per day. From fresh to frozen, crumbed to value-added products, Crest Choice Chicken produces over 50 different article lines. We are proud to supply the fresh poultry market with approximately 7 000 000 birds each year.
